To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the weak mixing angle sin2θW can be measured by neutrino-electronic scattering at a value Q ≃ 30 MeV with a precision 0.24% which is only a little bit larger than the one obtained by the LEP-I experiment at the Z-polar.

the weak mixing angle can be measured with an uncertainty of 0.3% by a neutrino beam dump at the CERN SPS, using the neutrino-electron elastic scattering channel, and a 100 kt water Cherenkov detector.

1) the neutrino source is an intense, clean, and stable source of ν¯e and νe; 2) a 100 kt Cerenkov detector can measure the neutrino cross-section at the 0.24% level; 3) the neutrino cross section can be extracted by a simple fit to a linear function; 4) the cross-section can be extracted without any assumptions on the underlying physics, in particular the value of sin2θW;
In summary, our research is concerned with

the possibility to measure the weak mixing angle sin2θW at a value of Q ≃ 30 MeV, using a proton beam dump with a 100 kt water Cerenkov neutrino detector, with a precision comparable to the one obtained by the LEP-I experiment at the Z-polar mass.
the study of the possibility of measuring the weak mixing angle sin2 θW at a precision of 1% at the energy scale Q = 30 MeV with neutrino-electrons scattering.
the possibility of a measurement of the weak angle with a precision of the order of 0.25% using neutrino-electron elastic scattering in a large water Cerenkov experiment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a measurement of sin2θW with a precision of better than 0.3% at Q ≃ 30 MeV is feasible with a neutrino-electron experiment at a muon beam dump, if a 100 kt water Cherenkov detector is used.
a measurement of sin2θW with a precision of better than 0.3% is possible at a neutrino-electron experiment at a low Q2 value.
the proposed experiment would be the first experiment to measure sin2 θ W at the Z-polar value with an uncertainty comparable to the one achieved at LEP-I.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the measurement of sin2θW with a precision of a factor three below LEP-I is possible with the proposed experiment.
we are able to reach the precision of 0, 24% for the sin2θW with the 100 kt scale detector.
a measurement of sin2θW with an error of about 0.24% is feasible at the neutrino factory, which is a factor 3 below the one obtained at LEP-I at Z-pole.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the precision achievable with neutrino-electronic scattering at low energy is comparable to the one achieved with the LEP-I experiment.
a measurement of the weak-mixing angle with neutrino scattering at low Q is feasible with a 10% precision, which is comparable with the current status.
the precision of a measurement of sin2θW at Q ≃ 30 MeV can be competitive with the one at the Z-polar mass and the main limitation to its improvement is the knowledge of the neutrino flux.
